Component 01 · Design layer

Homepage banner

Layout is unchanged from the signed-off wireframe: split below the navigation, static proposition on the left, rotating featured story on the right, dots in a fixed position, approximately 340px on desktop.

Imagery and story content are taken from the live banner. Each route is shown at its true 340px desktop height, in isolation — navigation and the content beneath have been stripped out so the comparison is only between the banners.

Route A

Editorial rule

Closest to the site today

White proposition panel, Midnight Blue display type, Merlot for the eyebrow and actions, and the brand horizon rule under the section. The quietest of the three and the least dependent on the colour rationalisation landing.

White surface Midnight Blue — display & body Merlot Red — eyebrow, CTA Espresso — rules
Desktop · banner 340px

  • 1The eyebrow carries the brand line. “Economics with imagination” is the core concept in the guidelines rather than a tagline, so it sits above the proposition as context rather than being set as a headline in its own right.
  • Type: display is Steelfish Extra Bold in all caps with the recommended letter-spacing; body and the story-card headline are Roboto. These prototypes substitute Oswald for Steelfish, which is a licensed font — the live build uses the real face.
  • Contrast: Midnight on white is 11.9:1 and Merlot on white is 8.4:1, both comfortably past AA. The story card sits on a solid white surface rather than relying on the image being dark enough, which is what the brief asks for.
Route B

Colour block

Boldest

The proposition panel becomes a solid Midnight Blue block running edge to edge with the navigation above it. Banana Yellow does the work of the accent. This is the option that makes the banner feel most deliberately redesigned rather than restyled.

Midnight Blue — surface Banana Yellow — accent White — text Midnight 90% — cards
Desktop · banner 340px

  • 2A dark story card instead of a white one. It reads as part of the same block as the left panel rather than as a label stuck on the photograph, and the Banana Yellow rule ties it to the CTA. White on Midnight is 11.9:1; Banana on Midnight is 7.6:1.
  • The colour does the separating. Navigation, banner and content sit on three distinct surfaces, so the overlap problem is solved structurally rather than by adding a border.
  • Worth weighing: a dark band at the top of every page is a significant change of character for the site, and the content immediately beneath it will have to work harder to feel like the same page. If the colour rationalisation lands on a lighter system, this route is the one most affected.
Route C

Soft tint

Closest to the admired reference

Grey Sky Blue tint behind the proposition, Peacock as the accent, and a rounded story card that sits over the image like the pill treatment Frontier liked. Warmer and more contemporary without leaving the palette.

Grey Sky 40% — surface Midnight Blue — display Peacock Blue — accent White — cards
Desktop · banner 340px

  • The rounded card is the one real departure from the current visual language. The guidelines describe lines, blocks and hard edges rather than rounded shapes, so this needs a conscious decision from the brand side rather than being slipped in.
  • Peacock on white is 5.7:1 — fine for the actions and eyebrows used here, but body copy stays Midnight rather than Peacock.
  • Common to all three routes: the panel rotates every 5.5 seconds, pauses on hover and on keyboard focus, and does not auto-rotate at all when the visitor has reduced-motion set. Dots are real buttons with labels and a visible focus ring.
Route D

Broadsheet

Alternative composition

The proposition is set as a masthead — Steelfish caps at around 66px, filling the left two thirds. The image narrows to a vertical plate on the right, and the rotating story moves out of the image entirely into a full-width bar beneath, where it reads as a strapline rather than a caption.

Paper Near-black — masthead, rules Merlot — kicker, dots Stone
Desktop · banner plus story bar, approx. 430px

  • 1The proposition finally gets the scale it deserves. The whole point of the banner change was making it clear what Frontier does above the fold; setting it as a masthead does that more forcefully than any amount of colour.
  • 2The story leaves the photograph. No overlay card, so no contrast risk over imagery and no dot-position problem — the bar is a fixed structure and the content inside it changes. It also means the image can be cropped freely without worrying about what sits on top of it.
  • What this changes against the wireframe: the banner is roughly 430px rather than 340px once the bar is included, and the story panel is no longer inside the image region. The rotation logic is unchanged.
Route E

Media card

Alternative composition

The left panel becomes a full brand-colour field with the Spark cropped into it, and the rotating story on the right is treated as a media card in its own tone. Closest thing here to how Frontier already presents itself on social and on report covers.

Midnight — proposition panel Banana — Spark, CTA Merlot — story tone Matcha — story tone

  • 3The Spark is used as the guidelines intend — large, cropped by the edge of the panel, sitting behind the type rather than floating as a logo. Its colourway changes with the panel tone.
  • 4The dots move into the horizon rule instead of sitting on the image, so they are in the same place on every story by construction rather than by matching heights.
  • What this changes against the wireframe: the story panel is now a full card that changes colour per story, not a white overlay on a photograph. The rotation and dot behaviour are identical; it is the surface that changed.
  • Worth testing with real content: a two-line caps headline is about the limit at this width. Anything longer needs the tone card to grow, which eats the image.
Responsive

Tablet and mobile

Route A shown at both breakpoints. The proposition stacks above the image so the value proposition is never pushed below a large photograph on mobile — the specific risk the brief calls out.

  • Stacking order is proposition first, story second at every width, matching the desktop reading order.
  • The story card stays inside the image region but loses its side insets on mobile so the headline keeps two full lines. Dots remain bottom-right of the card, in the same place on every story.
  • Minimum heights: the image region holds 260px on tablet and mobile so the crop stays legible; the banner itself is content-led rather than fixed once stacked.
  • Still to confirm with development: the final height rules and whether the existing carousel library supports this without a second library. Flagged in the brief as an open decision.
Design phase — three routes per component over the signed-off wireframe layouts. Colour and type from the Frontier Economics Visual Brand Guidelines 2023; content and imagery from frontier-economics.com. Oswald stands in for Steelfish in these prototypes.
